primitives.name: Pitch Control Pressure Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Pitch-control matrix**: for timestep t and pitch location (m,n), compute probability the defending team controls the ball there.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{control}(m,n,t)': 'Probability that the defending team controls the ball at location (m,n) at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Defending team's control probability is modeled via pitch control dynamics; spatial resolution fixed at 1 m.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pitch control model fails due to occlusion or inaccurate tracking data.

layer2.mapping: Maps defensive influence across pitch space using probabilistic control fields derived from player trajectories and velocities.
layer2.telemetry: Defensive zone occupancy rate, ball control likelihood per grid cell.

primitives.name: Vanilla Individual Pressure Vector
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Vanilla individual pressure matrix**: locate player, draw 1 m-diameter pressure circle, sample pitch-control pressure from 8 directions → 8-dim pressure vector.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{player}^{8}': '8-dimensional pressure vector for player at location (x,y)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pressure is isotropically distributed around player within 1 m radius; sampled from 8 compass directions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In cases of high player density or overlapping pressure circles.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to local pitch control field gradients, representing directional pressure intensity.
layer2.telemetry: Directional pressure magnitude, player proximity to ball zones.

primitives.name: Body Orientation Adjusted Pressure
primitives.verbatim_quote: **3D body-orientation extraction** (top-down from broadcast footage): detect player bounding boxes → 3D pose estimation per player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'O_{body}': '3D body orientation vector of player', 'P_{finetuned}': 'Adjusted pressure vector incorporating body orientation'}
primitives.assumptions: Body orientation reflects intent and influence; no geometric distortion assumed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When 3D pose estimation fails due to camera angle or motion blur.

layer2.mapping: Modulates vanilla pressure vector using body orientation to reflect directional intent.
layer2.telemetry: Orientation consistency, alignment with opponent movement.

The pitch control matrix defines a probabilistic landscape of ball control, while the vanilla pressure vector samples this landscape around players. Body orientation refines these vectors by weighting them according to player intent. These primitives form a layered structure where pitch control provides global context, vanilla pressure offers local granularity, and body orientation introduces behavioral nuance. Failure modes include misalignment between 3D pose and actual body orientation, or inaccuracies in pitch control modeling under occlusion. The system assumes that possession loss probability correlates with perceived pressure, which may not hold if non-pressure factors dominate.
